assessment: This article analyzes the mechanism of human pathogenicity linked to point mutations in the chromokinesin Kid/Kif22, that cause abnormal skeletal development. The authors show the mutations do not cause a loss of function. Instead, they are dominant negative and fail to inactivate the Kif22 motor, resulting in appropriate force generation of the motor during anaphase. This work highlights that the loss of regulation of kinesin motors in mitosis can disrupt cell division at the cellular scale and human pathogenesis.
